forecaster_note: Surfline's written forecast paragraph wasn't served this refresh — this note is generated by your surf agent straight from the raw Surfline model data. Saturday is the leftovers day: the tired S groundswell is down to 3.0ft @ 8s from 175° with a 2.1ft @ 7s ENE windswell underneath, 68 kJ at 9am and sliding to 52 by mid-afternoon. Dead south again, so Dee Why gives away a foot to Long Reef exactly like yesterday. W offshore (279°, 9 km/h) holds until about 11am, then a NE sea breeze takes over from noon and gets to 15 km/h gusting 27 by dusk — a genuine dawn-to-11am window and nothing after it. Sunday is the upgrade: a new E/NE swell arrives at 70–78°, 3.1ft @ 10s at dawn building to 3.5ft @ 9s and 128 kJ by noon, with NNW–NW offshore either side of a windy N patch around midday. Long Reef rates FAIR-GOOD across the whole of Sunday. Then Monday detonates — 645 kJ at 9am, Dee Why 4–6ft and Long Reef 6–8ft. — Surf Guru agent

days.label: Today
days.note: Dawn-to-11am or don't bother. W offshore 9 km/h holds through the 9:29am low, then the NE sea breeze owns the rest of the day and every spot drops to poor-fair. Swell is dead south (175°) again, so Dee Why is the small one — Long Reef is a clear foot bigger off identical 68 kJ.

swells.label: Dominant S swell — the angle Dee Why simply can't use
ENE windswell — this is what's actually feeding the banks
Faint 15s trace — occasional bigger set, not much else

dee-why.window: Dawn–10:30am. Offshore W 279° at 9 km/h, tide bottoming at 9:29am (0.49m) and filling after. Energy is already fading — 72 kJ at 6am, 68 at 9am, 60 by noon. Be out of the water before the NE fills in.
alerts: NE sea breeze from noon — rating drops to poor-fair everywhere for the whole afternoon

tip.label: Beachie, not the Point
tip.text: 175° is the direction the Point turns to mush — it'll be fat and gutless with no wall. The 2.1ft ENE windswell at 73° is the only thing with shape in it, so work the beachie banks. Save the frontside rights for tomorrow when the swell swings to 70°.

swells.label: Dominant S — Long Reef's best-exposed angle of the four

long-reef.window: Dawn–noon. Pick of the coast today and it holds its rating an hour longer than the others — still FAIR at midday while Dee Why and Manly have already dropped. 3–4ft on the sets early, easing to 2–3 after 11am.

tip.label: Take the drive
tip.text: Same 68 kJ as Dee Why, a whole foot more wave — that's exposure, not a rating artefact. You're backside on the lefts off the point, so set your line early off the take-off rather than chasing the end section down the bank.

curl-curl.window: Dawn–11am. Holds FAIR until noon then falls straight to POOR when the NE arrives — the sharpest afternoon drop of the four. South end picks up the S swell best.
alerts: Rated POOR from 3pm — worst afternoon on the coast today

tip.label: South corner
tip.text: With the swell at 175° the south end of the beach is the only part getting a straight shot at it. Half a foot bigger than Dee Why for the same energy, but Long Reef still beats it if you've got the drive in you.

swells.label: Dominant S swell — shadowed here, least of the four
ENE windswell — the useful component at North Steyne

manly.window: Dawn–10am only. Smallest of the four and it drops again in the afternoon — 1–2ft knee-to-thigh from 3pm. Only worth it if you're already in town.

tip.label: Skip it today
tip.text: North Steyne is shadowed from a 175° swell and there's no size to spare at 2–3ft. Nothing here that Long Reef isn't doing a foot better with the same wind.

days.label: Tomorrow
days.note: The angle finally turns. New E/NE swell at 70–78° — 3.1ft @ 10s at dawn building to 3.5ft @ 9s and 128 kJ by noon, nearly double today's energy. NNW offshore at 9am, a windy N patch around midday (15 gusting 25), then NW offshore again by 3pm. Long Reef rates FAIR-GOOD all day.

dee-why.window: 8–10:30am. The 70° E/NE angle is exactly what the Point wants, and NNW 334° is offshore at 8 km/h — but the model only gives Dee Why 2–3ft while Long Reef gets 3–4. Rating peaks FAIR at 9am then falls back to poor-fair once the N wind hits 15 gusting 25 around midday.
alerts: N wind 15 km/h gusting 25 around midday knocks it back — get in before 11am

tip.label: Frontside window
tip.text: This is your angle at the Point — 70° swinging to 78°, frontside rights, 92 kJ at 9am building to 128 by noon. Narrow window though: FAIR only at 9am. If the Point isn't working by 9:30 don't wait for it, drive to Long Reef.

long-reef.window: 9am–3pm — the widest good window of the weekend. FAIR-GOOD from 9am right through to 3pm, and the N wind that ruins Dee Why at midday stays offshore here. Waist-to-shoulder on the sets by noon at 128 kJ.

tip.label: Best call of the weekend
tip.text: Only spot rating FAIR-GOOD, and it holds it for six straight hours — no need to be up at dawn. Your 10am–12pm habit lands exactly on the 128 kJ peak. Backside lefts off the point again, but with a 9–10s period there's a real wall to work with this time.

curl-curl.window: All morning through mid-afternoon. Steady FAIR from dawn to dusk — no rating collapse at all tomorrow, and the wind stays offshore here through the midday N patch. A foot bigger than Dee Why.

tip.label: Solid backup
tip.text: Waist-to-chest at 92 kJ and completely stable all day — the low-risk option if you can't get out early. Not as good as Long Reef but it never drops below FAIR, which nowhere else manages except the Reef.

manly.window: Morning through mid-afternoon. FAIR from dawn to 3pm, dropping to poor-fair at dusk. Bigger than today thanks to the E/NE angle, but still the smallest of the four.

tip.label: In-town option
tip.text: The 70–78° angle suits North Steyne far better than today's south swell, so it's a real wave rather than a write-off. Still 2–3ft against Long Reef's 3–4 for the same energy — take it only if you're stuck in town.

days.label: Weekend
days.note: It's already Saturday, so this weekend is the two days above — and they're not the same wave. Saturday is a fading dead-south leftover with a hard NE cut-off at noon; Sunday brings a fresh E/NE swell at 70–78° with double the energy and offshore winds either side of a windy midday. If you only get one surf, make it Sunday mid-morning at Long Reef. And keep Monday clear: 645 kJ arrives at 9am with Dee Why at 4–6ft and Long Reef 6–8ft.

dee-why.window: Sunday 8–10:30am is the pick — right swell angle (70°), NNW offshore, 92 kJ building to 128. Saturday only works dawn–10:30am and the swell is the wrong direction for the Point.
alerts: Monday 10 Aug: 645 kJ at 9am, 4–6ft chest to 1ft overhead — a completely different day

tip.label: Sunday over Saturday
tip.text: Same spot, two different waves. Saturday's 175° swell won't wrap into the Point; Sunday's 70° will. If you can only surf once this weekend, take Sunday morning.

long-reef.window: Sunday 9am–3pm — the only FAIR-GOOD block of the weekend, six hours wide. Saturday it's still the biggest on the coast but only until noon.

tip.label: Weekend winner
tip.text: Biggest both days and the only spot rating above FAIR all weekend. Sunday mid-morning at 128 kJ is the session to plan around — and if Monday's 6–8ft interests you, this is where it'll be most rideable.

curl-curl.window: Sunday all day — rock steady FAIR dawn to dusk. Saturday, south corner only and be gone by noon (it drops to POOR from 3pm).

tip.label: Most consistent
tip.text: The least volatile spot of the weekend: no rating collapse on Sunday at all. Good insurance if a sleep-in kills your dawn plans.

manly.window: Sunday morning through 3pm. Saturday it's a dawn-only, 1–2ft-by-afternoon write-off.

tip.label: Convenience only
tip.text: Smallest of the four on both days. Sunday's E/NE angle at least makes it a real wave, but the drive north pays a full foot better.
